cause: Two distinct FP patterns. First: the parser treats entire articles or major sections as a single paragraph (77, 95, 107 sentences) when there are no blank-line separators, then attributes the violation to the first or last short sentence in that block ('This biography was unauthorized', 'Let's look at each of these in more detail.'). Second: legitimate dense paragraphs of 8-17 sentences in professional long-form articles are flagged by a threshold calibrated for blog posts. Neither pattern indicates slop.
fp_examples: [business/a16z] (Paragraph has 107 sentences. Keep paragraphs to 6 ) To receive this monthly update from the a16z fintech team, sign up here.
[business/a16z] (Paragraph has 95 sentences. Keep paragraphs to 6 s) Rather than relying solely on my anecdotal examples of 'important places,' I turned to LinkedIn.
[business/a16z] (Paragraph has 8 sentences. Keep paragraphs to 6 se) Last month, as CEO of SpiderNet, you were faced with the issue of firing your VP of Engineering...

cause: Flags topic-word repetition within a focused paragraph where repeating the subject is mandatory. Examples: 'interview' 9x and 'process' 11x in a paragraph about interviewing process; 'alfred' 14x in a biography of Alfred; 'company' 13x in a paragraph about company management; common function words ('will', 'with', 'from', 'this') flagged at 6-9x in long paragraphs. None of this is slop -- it is coherent, on-topic prose about a single subject.
fp_examples: [business/a16z] (Word repeated 14 times in one paragraph: 'alfred'.) This biography was unauthorized
[business/a16z] (Word repeated 11 times in one paragraph: 'process') Let's look at each of these in more detail.
[business/a16z] (Word repeated 9 times in one paragraph: 'this'. Ke) This biography was unauthorized

cause: Threshold of >1 exclamation mark per paragraph catches: proper nouns containing ! (Yahoo!, 'Tarzan Finds a Son!'), quoted speech combining multiple voices, colloquial vivid narration ('He went nuts!'), list headers used as rhetorical questions, and investment announcements with genuine enthusiasm. The 2 samples that approach TP territory have 6-9 exclamation marks in one paragraph but are energetic narrative writing, not boilerplate slop.
